title: Athena Fleet inference readiness playbook — latency, tail and cost sweep
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the Athena Fleet POC — objective is to qualify a hybrid inference deployment (hosted + dedicated burst) for a logistics customer whose workload mixes short chat-style prompts and long planning sequences. Focus areas: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail microbursts, warm vs cold KV-cache behavior, steady-state throughput, and cost per 1M tokens (hosted vs dedicated).

High-level goals:
- Verify p95 latency <= 220ms for chat path at mean length 64 tokens under steady QPS=150.
- Characterize tail (p99) under microbursts: 2x, 5x, 10x baseline for 30s windows.
- Measure cost delta for quantized model variants and with/without KV caching.
- Produce operational guidance: batching, autoscale windows, fallback model map.

Customer workload summary (from discovery):
- 70% short chat turns (user message ~20-80 tokens, expected response 40-120 tokens)
- 25% planning/docgen (single request with 600–1500 tokens output)
- 5% embeddings/rerank calls (small, latency-insensitive)
- Traffic profile: diurnal with sharp peaks at start/end of shifts; observed 10k QPS peaks in production sim -> for POC; emulate scaled down: baseline QPS=150, burst profiles described below.

Test harness & methodology:
- Harness: benchrunner-v3 (internal) driving the Redwood API. Runs across three host groups: hosted-prod (multi-tenant), dedicated-A100-40GB pool, dedicated-H100-80GB pool.
- Models used: redwood-mistral-13b-q4f16 (quantized), open-lms-14b-ggml (reference slow path), redwood-gptx-7b (fast chat variant).
- Sequences: short (mean 64 tokens request/80 tokens response), long (input 400 tokens / response 900 tokens).
- Cache modes: cold (new model container), warm-KV (cache primed by 1k representative prefixes), full-KV (cache primed by 10k unique prefixes).
- Batching settings swept: batch_size_limit = [1, 4, 8, 16]; batching_delay_ms = [0, 5, 20].
- Autoscale settings: probe scale-up threshold = 70% utilization, cooldown windows = [30s, 120s, 300s].
- Cost assumptions: GPU-hour list prices (A100-40 -> $2.40/hr, H100-80 -> $6.00/hr) plus fixed infra overhead (0.12 $/1M tokens for hosted baseline). These are modelled just for relative comparisons.

Key findings (summary):
- Short-chat steady state at QPS=150: dedicated-A100 with redwood-gptx-7b (batch_size_limit=4, delay=5ms) achieved p50=24ms, p95=110ms, p99=190ms. Hosted-prod p95 ~ 160ms for same model (higher multi-tenant variance) but had lower cost per M tokens for median volume due to sharing.
- Long plan requests: p95 dominated by generation time; H100-80 with redwood-mistral-13b-q4f16 was 1.8x faster than A100-40 in tokens/sec for long sequences, reducing p95 on 900-token outputs from ~6.2s -> ~3.5s.
- Tail behaviour under 5x microburst for 30s window: without KV-caching, p99 spiked to 2.1s on A100; with warm-KV the p99 reduced to 420ms. Most tail risk is cold KV initialization + model cold starts, not pure compute.
- Batching tradeoffs: larger batch sizes improve throughput (tokens/sec) but add median latency for single-turn requests. Batch_size_limit=4 with 5ms delay is a sweet spot for mixed workloads.
- Autoscale cooldown: 30s cooldown led to thrashing under repeated microbursts; 120s was a reasonable compromise. 300s delayed recovery and elevated queued latency.
- Cost: quantized redwood-mistral-13b-q4f16 reduced GPU-hours by ~34% for long workloads vs fp16; on dedicated fleet this translated to ~22% lower cost per 1M tokens after accounting for lower throughput on A100 vs H100. Hosted pricing still cheaper at low sustained volume (<50k tokens/day) because infra amortization.

Representative numbers (steady chat path, QPS=150):
- dedicated-A100 (gptx-7b, batch=4, delay=5ms): p50 24ms, p95 110ms, p99 190ms, throughput ~56k tokens/min, est cost per 1M tokens: $18.3
- hosted-prod (gptx-7b): p50 30ms, p95 160ms, p99 340ms, throughput ~60k tokens/min, est cost per 1M tokens: $14.7
- dedicated-H100 (mistral-13b-q4f16, long path): p50 1500ms, p95 3500ms, p99 5200ms for 900-token outputs; tokens/sec ~220 vs A100 ~125

Operational recommendations (for customer):
1) Hybrid routing: route chat traffic to dedicated-A100 pool with reserved capacity; route long planning jobs to dedicated-H100 when latency for long jobs matters, else fall back to hosted with higher throughput. Implement automatic model variant mapping (gptx-7b for chat, mistral-13b-q4f16 for heavy generation).
2) KV-cache priming: add a warmup run during deploys that primes the top 5k prefixes (based on customer prompt taxonomy) to reduce tail during rollouts.
3) Batching defaults: set batch_size_limit=4 and batching_delay=5ms for mixed customer workloads. Allow config overrides per route.
4) Autoscale: scale-up threshold 70% util, scale-down with 120s cooldown, minimum warm workers = 2 per shard to tolerate short bursts.
5) Fallback policies: if dedicated pool latency > p95 threshold for 60s, automatically fallback to hosted-prod model variant with lower variance.
6) Cost control: use quantized variants for heavy long-job routes and enforce per-route token quotas for ad-hoc long generations.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Need to validate real customer prefix distribution; current prefixes are synthetic. Planned dataset from customer expected 2028-09-02 (ticket JIRA-ENG-3499).
- Evaluate wake-up cost of on-prem private deployments (HSM/KMS integration delays) — not covered in this sweep.
- Long-term: run multi-day soak with realistic diurnal pattern and intermittent failures to validate autoscale heuristics and fallback frequency.

Appendix: experimental notes and rough checklist:
- Drive: benchrunner-v3 config used: bench/athena/sweep-aug28.yaml (see linked GH PR).
- Raw logs: sheets://1A2bAthenaSweepResults (tab: raw-latency), sheet contains sample-by-sample latencies and lossless traces.
- Quick wins for next week: add automated KV-primer job, add a probe to detect cold-container starts and log cause, test scale cooldown 120s in canary.

Meeting notes (workshop 2028-08-22 with customer):
- Customer priority: predictable p95 for chat during shift start windows. They accept longer tails for batch planning jobs.
- Security ask: VPC egress restrictions - implies dedicated pools or Private deployment. Discuss pricing delta.
- Action items: Solutions engineering to deliver a 2-week pilot with reserved A100 pool + routing rules; CS to draft commercial delta.

End of playbook (working doc) — expect iterations as we get real prefix data and run soak tests.
